chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: The Willy Lewis seasonal circuit and picking up languages
summary: The band wintered in France, spent spring in Egypt and summer at Knokke, Belgium, and Butler used Creole with West Indians to pick up French.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I went to school and was studying, started studying right away. Now, here in wintertime we would stay there in France. Now, when you come into spring, we'd go to Egypt. And the summertime, we'd go to Knokke, Belgium. And in the fall we'd go to -- we'd go in between Knokke (PHONETIC) and we might go to Portugal then. So that was the routine. Recording new things, you see.
So you began to pick up French then while you were there?

Being around, (inaudible) and then, especially I was hanging out with the antilliads, the people from Haiti and Guadalupe. So naturally, I was speaking Creole and they're speaking the same thing. So then the Guadalupians and Creole people and also the Cubans. And then later on I began to hang out with the other people, see. I could have
out with Americans all the time and not speak nothing, see. But I didn't see it that way.
